```{r}
#' Create and train XGBoost model for traffic imputation
#'
#' This function creates and trains an XGBoost model for imputing missing traffic data.
#'
#' @param data A preprocessed data frame containing traffic data.
#' @param target Character. The target variable to impute.
#' @param base_vars Character vector. Base variables used for prediction.
#' @param threshold_uptime Numeric. Threshold for uptime to determine missing values.
#'
#' @return A data frame with imputed values and imputation flags.
#'
#' @importFrom dplyr select mutate bind_rows %>%
#' @importFrom stats complete.cases na.omit
#' @importFrom xgboost xgboost xgb.DMatrix predict
#'
#' @examples
#' # Assuming 'traffic' is your dataset
#' data <- validate_and_preprocess_data(data = traffic, 
#'                                      transport_type = "car",
#'                                      sensors_id = 9000001844,
#'                                      base_vars = c("day_of_month","hour","weekday","month","year","vacation","week_number","segment_id","date"))
#'                                      
#' data <- create_and_train_model(data = data, 
#'                                target = "car",
#'                                base_vars = c("day_of_month","hour","weekday","month","year","vacation","week_number","segment_id","date"),
#'                                threshold_uptime = 0.5)

create_and_train_model <- function(data, target, base_vars, threshold_uptime) {
  library(caret)  # Pour one-hot encoding

  # Prepare data for XGBoost
  data_xgb <- data %>%
    mutate(y = ifelse(.data$uptime < threshold_uptime,
                      NA, !!sym(target))) %>% 
    select(-!!sym(target))

  # Split data into training and imputation sets
  is_train <- !is.na(data_xgb$y)
  data_train <- data_xgb[is_train,]
  data_imput <- data_xgb[!is_train,]

  # Remove NA from training data
  data_train_clean <- data_train %>%
    select(.data$y, all_of(base_vars)) %>%
    na.omit()

  # Function to prepare data for XGBoost
  prepare_data_for_xgboost <- function(df) {
    df <- df %>%
      mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
    
    # Identify non-numeric columns
    non_numeric_cols <- sapply(df, function(x) !is.numeric(x))
    
    if(any(non_numeric_cols)) {
      # Apply one-hot encoding to non-numeric columns
      dummy <- dummyVars(" ~ .", data = df[, non_numeric_cols, drop = FALSE])
      encoded_df <- predict(dummy, newdata = df[, non_numeric_cols, drop = FALSE])
      
      # Combine encoded columns with numeric columns
      df <- cbind(df[, !non_numeric_cols, drop = FALSE], encoded_df)
    }
    
    return(df)
  }

  # Prepare training data
  data_train_clean <- prepare_data_for_xgboost(data_train_clean)

  # Prepare data for XGBoost
  train_matrix <- xgb.DMatrix(data = as.matrix(select(data_train_clean, -y)),
                              label = data_train_clean$y)

  # Set XGBoost parameters
  params <- list(
    objective = "reg:squarederror",
    eta = 0.3,
    max_depth = 6,
    min_child_weight= 3,

    nrounds = 100
  )

  # Train XGBoost model
  model_xgb <- xgboost(data = train_matrix,
                       params = params,
                       nrounds = params$nrounds,
                       verbose = 0)

  # Prepare imputation data
  data_imput_clean <- data_imput %>%
    select(all_of(base_vars))

  data_imput_clean <- prepare_data_for_xgboost(data_imput_clean)

  rows_to_predict <- complete.cases(data_imput_clean)

  # Make predictions only for complete cases
  if (any(rows_to_predict)) {
    imput_matrix <- xgb.DMatrix(data = as.matrix(data_imput_clean[rows_to_predict,]))
    predictions <- predict(model_xgb, imput_matrix)

    # Assign predictions back to the original imputation data frame
    data_imput$y <- NA
    data_imput$y[rows_to_predict] <- predictions
  }

  # Combine results
  result <- bind_rows(
    data_train %>% mutate(imputed = "original"),
    data_imput %>% mutate(imputed = "imputed")
  )

  names(result)[names(result) == "y"] <- target

  return(result)
}
```

```{r}
library(xgboost)
library(caret)
library(dplyr)

fine_tune_xgboost <- function(data_imput, target, base_vars) {
  # Préparer les données
  data_tune <- data_imput %>%
    select(all_of(c(target, base_vars))) %>%
    na.omit() %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor),
           across(where(is.factor), as.numeric),
           across(everything(), as.numeric))
  
  # Créer la matrice DMatrix
  dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = as.matrix(select(data_tune, -all_of(target))),
                        label = data_tune[[target]])
  
  # Définir la grille de paramètres (réduite pour plus de rapidité)
  param_grid <- expand.grid(
    eta = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3),
    max_depth = c(3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
    min_child_weight = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
    subsample = c(0.7, 0.8, 0.9),
    colsample_bytree = c(0.7, 0.8, 0.9)
  )
  
  # Fonction pour effectuer la validation croisée
  cv_function <- function(params) {
    params_list <- as.list(params)
    params_list$objective <- "reg:squarederror"
    
    cv_results <- xgb.cv(
      params = params_list,
      data = dtrain,
      nrounds = 100,
      nfold = 5,
      early_stopping_rounds = 10,
      verbose = 0
    )
    
    return(min(cv_results$evaluation_log$test_rmse_mean))
  }
  
  # Appliquer la fonction de validation croisée à chaque combinaison de paramètres
  results <- apply(param_grid, 1, cv_function)
  
  # Trouver la meilleure combinaison de paramètres
  best_params <- param_grid[which.min(results), ]
  
  # Préparer les meilleurs paramètres pour le modèle final
  best_params_list <- as.list(best_params)
  best_params_list$objective <- "reg:squarederror"
  
  # Entraîner le modèle final avec les meilleurs paramètres
  best_model <- xgboost(
    params = best_params_list,
    data = dtrain,
    nrounds = 100,
    early_stopping_rounds = 10,
    verbose = 0
  )
  
  return(list(best_model = best_model, best_params = best_params))
}

# Utilisation de la fonction
result <- fine_tune_xgboost(data_imput, target = "vehicle", 
                            base_vars = c("day_of_month", "hour", "weekday", "month", "year", 
                                          "vacation", "week_number", "segment_id", "date"))

# Afficher les meilleurs paramètres
print(result$best_params)
```
```{r}
base_vars = c("day_of_month", "hour", "weekday", "month", "year", 
                                          "vacation", "week_number", "segment_id", "date")



data_train <- data_imput[!is.na(data_imput$vehicle),] %>% select(all_of(c("vehicle", base_vars)))

data_test <- data_imput[is.na(data_imput$vehicle),] %>% select(all_of(c("vehicle", base_vars)))

# Convert weekday to factor
data_train$weekday <- as.factor(data_train$weekday)
data_test$weekday <- as.factor(data_test$weekday)

# Ensure all categorical variables are factors
categorical_vars <- c("weekday", "month", "vacation", "segment_id")
for (var in categorical_vars) {
  data_train[[var]] <- as.factor(data_train[[var]])
  data_test[[var]] <- as.factor(data_test[[var]])
}
val_reel[["segment_id"]] <- as.factor(val_reel[["segment_id"]])

# Now run your GBM model
set.seed(321)
library(gbm)
library(dplyr)

shrinkage <- c(0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1)
n_trees <- c(100, 500, 1000, 5000)
results <- data.frame()
models_list <- list()

for (i in 1:length(shrinkage)) {
  for (j in 1:length(n_trees)) {
    model <- gbm(vehicle ~ . - date,
                 data = data_train,
                 distribution = "gaussian",
                 shrinkage = shrinkage[i],
                 n.trees = n_trees[j],
                 bag.fraction = 0.5)
    
    best_iter <- gbm.perf(model, plot.it = FALSE, method = "OOB")
    
    data_test$predictions <- predict(model, data_test, n.trees = best_iter)
    rmse_df <- data_test %>%
      left_join(val_reel, by = c("date", "segment_id")) %>%
      mutate(error = vehicle_reel - predictions) %>%
      summarise(rmse = sqrt(mean(error^2, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
      mutate(shrinkage = shrinkage[i], n_trees = n_trees[j])
    
    results <- bind_rows(results, rmse_df)
    
    model_name <- paste("shrinkage:", shrinkage[i], "n_trees:", n_trees[j])
    models_list[[model_name]] <- model
  }
}

# Trier les résultats par RMSE
results <- results %>% arrange(rmse)

# Afficher les résultats
print(results)

# Identifier le meilleur modèle
best_model <- results[1,]
print("Meilleur modèle :")
print(best_model)

# Tracer un graphique récapitulatif
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(results, aes(x = as.factor(n_trees), y = rmse, color = as.factor(shrinkage))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "RMSE par nombre d'arbres et taux d'apprentissage",
       x = "Nombre d'arbres", y = "RMSE", color = "Taux d'apprentissage") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#Determinier le meilleur shrinkage
```{r}
# Set the grid of hyperparameters
n_trees <- 2785
shrinkage <- 0.5 #c(0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1)
interaction.depth = seq(2,5)
results <- data.frame()
models_list <- list()

for (i in 1:length(interaction.depth)) {
  model <- gbm(vehicle ~ . - date,
               data = data_train,
               distribution = "gaussian",
               shrinkage = shrinkage,
               n.trees = n_trees,
               interaction.depth = interaction.depth[i],
               bag.fraction = 0.5)
  
  #best_iter <- gbm.perf(model, plot.it = FALSE,method= "OOB")
  predictions <- predict(model, data_test, n.trees = n_trees)
  
  
  
  model_name <- paste("depth:", interaction.depth[i])
  models_list[[model_name]] <- model
  
   
  data_test$predictions <- predict(model, data_test, n.trees = best_iter)
  rmse <- data_test %>%
    left_join(val_reel, by = c("date", "segment_id")) %>%
    mutate(error = abs(vehicle_reel - predictions)))
    print(rmse$error)
     rmse <- rmse %>%  summarise(rmse = sqrt(mean(error^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
              mae = mean(error,na.rm=T)) %>% mutate(shrinkage = shrinkage[i], n_trees = n_trees[j]) %>% pull(mae)
  
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
    model_param = model_name,
    shrinkage = shrinkage,
    n_trees = n_trees,
    mae = rmse
  ))
}

results

shrinkage <- 0.5
```
